title: Tilted camera mount on a datum plane
prompt: Desk mount for a small camera: a 60 × 40 × 5 mm base (X from −30 to 30, Y from 0 to 40, top face on Z = 0) and a 60 × 50 × 5 mm plate hinged on the base's front top edge (the X axis) that leans back over the base at 60° from horizontal, its front face starting on that edge and the plate joined to the base. Two M3 clearance holes through the plate, 20 mm apart (X = ±10) and 35 mm up the plate from the edge. Make the lean angle a parameter called tilt.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Base and plate are one solid
Base from Z = −5, front edge on Y = 0
Two Ø3.4 holes 35 mm up the plate, at X = ±10
tilt = 75 raises the plate top to 50·sin 75° = 48.30 mm

notes: The plate's front face lies on the plane through the X axis at 60° (a datum plane: XZ rotated by tilt − 90 about X); the plate is 5 thick behind it, so its lower end dips into the base (overlap 60·∫₀⁵ t/tan 60° dt = 433.0 mm³).
